experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most iconic gourmet markets located in the historic center. Sample local cheeses, exotic meats, fresh juices, and traditional Mexican street food. Ideal for Day 2 morning after a late Day 1 arrival, and within walking distance of centrally located hotels in Centro Histórico.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Explore her personal belongings, artwork, and the vibrant cultural history of one of Mexico's most celebrated artists. Book tickets in advance. Stay in Coyoacán or Roma Sur to minimize travel time.

experiences.name: Tacos and Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Spend an evening hopping between acclaimed taco stands and mezcalerías in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood. Try al pastor, suadero, and carnitas tacos paired with artisanal mezcal. This neighborhood is a top hotel hub, making it easy to access on any evening including Day 1 after a late arrival.

experiences.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning guided group tour to the ancient Aztec pyramids of Teotihuacán, including the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon. Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat. Many tours depart from Centro Histórico or Reforma, making hotel proximity key. Schedule for Day 3 or 4.
experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (day trip from Centro Histórico)

experiences.name: Lucha Libre Wrestling Show at Arena México
experiences.description: Experience the electrifying spectacle of Mexican Lucha Libre wrestling at the legendary Arena México. Enjoy colorful masked wrestlers, passionate crowds, and authentic street food vendors outside the arena. Located near Centro Histórico, ideal for an evening activity mid-trip on Day 3 or 4.
experiences.location: Doctores, Centro Histórico area, Mexico City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Metro Line 5 from the airport to the city center (very budget-friendly at ~5 MXN). Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walking tour of the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the magnificent Catedral Metropolitana (free entry). Stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero, beautifully lit in the evening. Visit the rooftop of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a free peek at the stunning Tiffany stained-glass ceiling in the lobby. Wind down with a walk around the illuminated Zócalo.

meals.lunch: Grab affordable tacos or a torta from street vendors near the Zócalo for around 50–80 MXN. Look for stands with long local queues — a sure sign of quality.
meals.dinner: Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén or a nearby fondita (family-run eatery) for a comida corrida (set meal: soup, main, drink) for around 80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your luggage light and use the Metro from the airport — it's the cheapest and fastest option. Validate your Metro card for multiple uses. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport or use a local ATM for best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its museum (entry ~80 MXN). This ancient Aztec temple is right next to the Zócalo and offers incredible insight into pre-Hispanic Mexico City. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ruins and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (free to enter the ground floor and admire the exterior). Then walk to the Alameda Central park for a relaxing stroll among locals. Visit the Museo Mural Diego Rivera next to the park (entry ~45 MXN) to see the famous 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon' mural.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Barrio Lagunilla area and browse the evening street market atmosphere. Head back toward Centro for a relaxed evening exploring the illuminated colonial streets.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local market breakfast stall near your hotel — try chilaquiles or tamales with atole for 50–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Street tacos near Templo Mayor or a market stall lunch — try tacos de canasta (basket tacos) for around 15–20 MXN each.
meals.dinner: Restaurante El Cardenal (Centro branch) offers authentic Mexican cuisine at moderate prices, or opt for a fondita nearby for 100–150 MXN for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Palacio de Bellas Artes hosts free cultural events and exhibitions on the upper floors on Sundays. Check their schedule if visiting on a Sunday — entry to permanent collections may be free.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (Line 3 to Viveros station, ~5 MXN). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo — La Casa Azul (entry ~270 MXN, book online in advance). This is one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural experiences and well worth the splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Coyoacán neighborhood on foot — visit the cobblestone Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, browse the artisan market stalls, and soak in the bohemian atmosphere. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for fresh food and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Visit the Mercado de Artesanías near the Zócalo for souvenir browsing. Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere of the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Centro before heading out — try pan dulce and café de olla for 40–60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat inside Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas for 60–100 MXN. This is one of the best budget food experiences in the city.
meals.dinner: Tacos al pastor from a popular taquería in Centro Histórico — many open late and serve excellent tacos for 20–25 MXN each.

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets online at least a few days in advance — it sells out quickly. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive, so comfortable shoes are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Metro + bus or Metrobús to Xochimilco (use Line 2 Metro then transfer). Enjoy a trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) ride through the ancient Aztec canals — negotiate a group rate or join others to share a boat (around 300–400 MXN per hour per boat, split among passengers). This is a UNESCO World Heritage experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Mercado Jamaica — a massive, colorful flower market that's a feast for the senses and completely free to explore. Browse the stalls of exotic blooms, fruits, and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Plaza Garibaldi, the famous mariachi square in Centro, about a 15-minute walk from your hotel. Enjoy free live mariachi performances in the square — musicians play for tips and for paying customers at surrounding pulquerías and cantinas.

meals.breakfast: Grab tamales and atole from a street cart near the Metro station before departing — a classic Mexico City breakfast for 40–60 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at the food stalls near Xochimilco's embarcadero — try fresh fish tacos, tlayudas, or elotes for 60–100 MXN.
meals.dinner: Have dinner at a cantina near Plaza Garibaldi — many offer free botanas (bar snacks) with drink purchases. A beer costs around 50–70 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best visited on weekdays to avoid large crowds and higher boat prices. Negotiate firmly with boat operators before boarding. Keep valuables secure in busy market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest museums (entry ~85 MXN). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the pre-Hispanic civilizations of Mexico, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — one of the largest urban parks in the world and completely free. Enjoy the lakes, paths, and local families enjoying their day. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec on the hilltop for panoramic city views (entry ~85 MXN).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping at street markets near the Zócalo. Enjoy a farewell dinner celebrating the best of Mexican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full Mexican breakfast at a local café near the hotel — huevos rancheros or molletes with coffee for 80–120 MXN.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a nearby market or street stalls in Chapultepec park — grab fresh fruit, elotes (corn), and snacks for 60–80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — try Mercado de Medellín or a well-reviewed local restaurant in Centro for pozole, mole, or chiles en nogada for 150–200 MXN. A memorable farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is free on Sundays for Mexican nationals, but foreign visitors still pay. The Bosque de Chapultepec is massive — wear comfortable walking shoes. Keep Metro cards topped up for easy transport throughout the day.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approx. 45–60 min by metro or taxi). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Catedral Metropolitana. Soak in the atmosphere of the historic heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero, lit up beautifully in the early evening. Head to the rooftop bar at Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a drink with stunning views over the Zócalo before dinner.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or upon arrival: try a torta or tacos from a street stall near the hotel for around 80–120 MXN.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Palma 23, Centro Histórico) — a beloved mid-range institution serving classic Mexican cuisine. Try the mole, chiles en nogada (seasonal), and freshly made tortillas. Budget ~350–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency or withdraw pesos at the airport. Use authorized taxis or the AICM app for safe transport. Keep valuables secure in Centro Histórico.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history — free entry with ID. Then walk to the Templo Mayor archaeological site, the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, with its excellent on-site museum (~80 MXN entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mercado de San Juan (20-min walk or short metro ride) for a deep dive into local food culture — sample cheeses, exotic fruits, charcuterie, and international ingredients. Afterward, visit the Museo de Arte Popular (MAP) nearby to discover traditional Mexican crafts and folk art (~60 MXN entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the charming Barrio de La Merced area or take a taxi to Plaza Garibaldi to experience live Mariachi music in an authentic setting. Enjoy the lively street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba (Tacuba 28, Centro Histórico) — a historic café open since 1912. Try tamales, atole, and fresh-squeezed juice. ~150–250 MXN per person.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan — graze on market stalls. Try tlayudas, fresh ceviche, or a torta ahogada. ~100–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Cantina La Peninsular near Plaza Garibaldi — traditional cantina food with free botanas (bar snacks) with drinks. Try the pozole or birria. ~200–350 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays. Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant walking on cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán (approx. 1 hour by bus from Terminal Central del Norte). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds. Entry ~80 MXN; bus ~50 MXN each way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city by early afternoon. Stop at the neighborhood of Tlatelolco on the way back to see the Plaza de las Tres Culturas — a poignant site blending Aztec ruins, a colonial church, and modern architecture (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Relax and refresh at the hotel, then explore the nightlife and culture of Centro Histórico. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior and lobby are free) illuminated at night — a stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco landmark.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pan dulce and café de olla from a local panadería near the hotel before heading to the bus terminal. ~50–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: At Teotihuacán, dine at La Gruta — a restaurant set inside a natural cave near the archaeological site. Mid-range Mexican classics like mole and enchiladas. ~300–450 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (Isabel la Católica 30, Centro Histórico) — elegant courtyard restaurant serving refined Mexican regional cuisine. Try the chiles rellenos or the mole negro. ~400–600 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start the Teotihuacán day early (depart by 8:00 AM) to avoid midday heat. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Buses to Teotihuacán depart from Terminal Autobuses del Norte (Metro: Autobuses del Norte, Line 5).

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3) to Coyoacán — a bohemian, colonial neighborhood. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul), the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book tickets online in advance (~250 MXN). Stroll through the colorful streets afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Museo León Trotsky (former home and final resting place of the exiled revolutionary, ~50 MXN). Then browse the weekend Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for handicrafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Relax in the Jardín Centenario plaza.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the underground mezcal and cocktail bar scene. Visit Bósforo (Luis Moya 31) — a legendary mezcalería with a great selection of artisanal mezcals in a cool speakeasy atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café in Centro before heading out.
meals.lunch: Los Danzantes (Jardín Centenario 12, Coyoacán) — popular mid-range restaurant with a lovely courtyard, known for Oaxacan-inspired cuisine and mezcal cocktails. Try the tlayuda or mole. ~300–450 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Taquería El Califa de León (near Centro) — legendary taquería, home of the world's first Michelin-starred taco (Gaonera taco). Simple, outstanding, affordable. ~150–250 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before your trip. Coyoacán is especially lively on weekends with street performers and markets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world, housing extraordinary collections of pre-Columbian artifacts including the Aztec Sun Stone. (~85 MXN entry). Spend at least 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) atop the hill for panoramic city views and fascinating Mexican imperial history (~85 MXN entry). Wind down with a walk through the park.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the city — return to Centro Histórico for a farewell dinner. Browse the illuminated streets of the historic center one last time and pick up any last-minute souvenirs along Calle Moneda or near the Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: Café Jekemir (República de Uruguay, Centro) — a beloved local breakfast spot. Try huevos rancheros, chilaquiles, or molletes with fresh juice. ~150–200 MXN per person.
meals.lunch: Contramar (Durango 200, Roma Norte — a short taxi/Uber from Chapultepec) — iconic Mexico City seafood restaurant. Famous for the tuna tostadas and red-and-green grilled fish. ~500–700 MXN per person — a splurge-worthy final lunch.
meals.dinner: Casa de los Azulejos (Madero 4, Centro Histórico) — a stunning 16th-century tiled mansion housing a classic restaurant. Enjoy traditional Mexican dishes in a breathtaking historic setting. ~300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is closed on Mondays. If departing the next day, pack bags the night before. Keep Uber or taxi apps ready for efficient airport transfer. Tip: 10–15% is standard at sit-down restaurants in Mexico City.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via private luxury transfer. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation walk through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Visit the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral (Catedral Metropolitana) and admire its baroque façade. Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian boulevard lined with colonial architecture, and stop at the iconic Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles) for a quick look.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop cocktail experience at one of Centro Histórico's acclaimed rooftop bars overlooking the Zócalo at dusk. Enjoy panoramic views of the illuminated historic skyline before heading to dinner.

meals.lunch: Azul Histórico: An elegant courtyard restaurant inside a colonial mansion on Uruguay Street. Known for refined regional Mexican cuisine. Try the mole negro and fresh ceviche.
meals.dinner: Limosneros: A celebrated fine-dining restaurant steps from the hotel, serving contemporary Mexican cuisine rooted in pre-Hispanic and colonial culinary traditions. Book the tasting menu with mezcal pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer for a seamless arrival experience. Request an early check-in if possible. Carry light clothing as March afternoons in Mexico City are typically warm (18–24°C), with cool evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum. This Aztec ceremonial center was discovered beneath Centro Histórico and offers extraordinary insight into Mexica civilization. A knowledgeable private archaeologist-guide will bring the ruins to life with stories of ritual, cosmology, and conquest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) to marvel at Diego Rivera's breathtaking murals depicting the history of Mexico — a UNESCO-recognized masterpiece of public art. Afterward, explore the nearby Mercado de San Juan, a gourmet market beloved by local chefs, where you can sample artisan cheeses, imported delicacies, and exotic fruits.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance of traditional Mexican music or a folkloric dance show at the Palacio de Bellas Artes (Palace of Fine Arts), one of the most beautiful Art Nouveau buildings in the Americas. Check the evening program in advance for the Ballet Folklórico de México.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the boutique hotel's dining space or nearby Café de Tacuba, a legendary restaurant open since 1912 serving traditional Mexican breakfasts including chilaquiles, tamales, and café de olla.
meals.lunch: El Cardinal: A Mexico City institution in Centro Histórico, renowned for its traditional Mexican fare including consommé, carnitas, and freshly made tortillas pressed tableside.
meals.dinner: Pujol (reserve well in advance): Chef Enrique Olvera's flagship restaurant, consistently ranked among the world's best. The iconic Mole Madre — a mole aged over 1,000 days — is an unmissable culinary experience. Located in Polanco, a short luxury taxi ride from the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Book Templo Mayor private guide and Pujol reservation well in advance. Palacio de Bellas Artes tickets for evening performances should be secured at least a day ahead. Dress smart-casual for Pujol.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient city of pyramids located approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Depart early by private chauffeured vehicle. Enjoy an exclusive sunrise or early-morning access tour of the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with a private archaeologist guide. Explore the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop en route at a traditional pulquería or artisan mezcal producer for a tasting session. Back in Centro Histórico, visit the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) for an immersive journey through five centuries of Mexican fine art, housed in a stunning neoclassical building.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at the rooftop terrace of Gran Hotel Ciudad de México, overlooking the Zócalo with its spectacular Tiffany stained-glass dome visible from the lobby. Wind down with a private mezcal tasting curated by a sommelier at your hotel or a nearby specialty bar.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the hotel or a quick stop at a local panadería (bakery) before departure to Teotihuacán.
meals.lunch: La Gruta Restaurant at Teotihuacán: A unique dining experience inside a natural cave adjacent to the pyramids. Enjoy traditional Mexican cuisine — mole, enchiladas, and slow-cooked meats — in an atmospheric underground setting.
meals.dinner: Contramar: An iconic Mexico City seafood restaurant (short drive from Centro Histórico). Famous for its tuna tostadas and the signature grilled fish with red and green salsa. A beloved institution among locals and international food lovers alike.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 7:00–7:30 AM to enjoy cooler temperatures and fewer crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection. The site involves significant walking and stair climbing. Confirm Contramar reservation in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private immersive cooking class with a renowned local chef specializing in traditional Mexican cuisine. Learn to prepare dishes such as mole, tamales, and salsas from scratch using ingredients sourced from a morning visit to a local market. Classes are typically held in beautifully designed kitchen studios in or near Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán (approximately 30 minutes by private car). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul — Blue House), the former home of the iconic Mexican artist, filled with her personal belongings, artwork, and vibrant gardens. Stroll through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets, artisan markets, and colorful plazas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Enjoy a private mezcal and tequila masterclass at a curated spirits bar, guided by an expert sommelier exploring the nuances of agave-based spirits from different Mexican regions. Follow with a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to Mercado de San Juan for fresh juices, tropical fruits, and artisan pastries — a quintessential Mexico City morning ritual.
meals.lunch: El Jardín del Pulpo in Coyoacán or Los Danzantes Coyoacán, an upscale restaurant in the heart of Coyoacán's main plaza serving contemporary Oaxacan cuisine with an exceptional mezcal menu.
meals.dinner: Quintonil: Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant in Polanco, ranked among Latin America's best. Focuses on native Mexican ingredients and seasonal produce with a modern, sophisticated approach. Pair with their curated wine and spirits list.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and Museo Frida Kahlo tickets in advance — the Blue House has timed entry and sells out quickly, especially on weekends. Quintonil requires advance reservations. Consider a private car for the Coyoacán excursion for comfort and flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Centro Histórico. Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor one more time or explore the nearby Museo de la Ciudad de México (Museum of Mexico City), housed in a stunning 18th-century palace. Browse curated artisan shops along República de Uruguay and Moneda streets for premium souvenirs including Talavera ceramics, handwoven textiles, and fine silver jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a luxury spa treatment at one of Mexico City's top hotel spas (such as the Four Seasons or St. Regis, both a short drive away) for a restorative pre-departure experience. Alternatively, take a private guided street food tour through the historic center, visiting legendary taquerías, torta stands, and chocolate shops for a final deep dive into Mexico City's extraordinary culinary street culture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a landmark restaurant. Enjoy cocktails and a final sunset view over the city before heading to the airport or retiring for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba for a nostalgic final traditional Mexican breakfast — café de olla, pan dulce, and huevos rancheros in a colonial setting that has served guests since 1912.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan gourmet market lunch — graze through stalls offering fresh oysters, artisan charcuterie, exotic cheeses, and freshly prepared Mexican specialties for a casual yet premium final midday meal.
meals.dinner: Don Chon: A legendary and historic restaurant in Tepito/Centro Histórico area, specializing in pre-Hispanic Mexican cuisine. Try dishes featuring huitlacoche (corn truffle), escamoles (ant larvae), and other ancestral ingredients — a truly unique and unforgettable final dining experience in Mexico City.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Mexico City traffic can be heavy, especially in the late afternoon. Arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Confirm all souvenir purchases comply with customs regulations. Consider tipping generously as service culture is deeply valued in Mexico City's hospitality industry.
